content: A chancre is a painless ulceration that develops during the primary stage of syphilis. This lesion typically appears approximately 21 days after the initial exposure to Treponema pallidum, a gram-negative spirochete bacterium responsible for causing syphilis. Chancres serve as a source of transmission for syphilis, a sexually transmitted infection, through direct physical contact. These ulcers most commonly form on or around the anus, mouth, penis, and vagina. Chancres may resolve spontaneously within three to six weeks without the use of medical treatment. Additionally, chancres are also associated with African trypanosomiasis, commonly known as sleeping sickness, which occurs following the bite of a tsetse fly. Pathological findings include the presence of chancres (pronounced shang-ker) on the penis as a result of a primary syphilitic infection.
